newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Former Zaire PM resurfaces in Geneva.
newsitem.headline: Former Zaire PM resurfaces in Geneva.

text.p: Zaire's former prime minister Kengo wa Dondo, who is wanted in his capital Kinshasa, on Wednesday resurfaced in Geneva where he said he was undergoing medical checks, Swiss news agency ATS reported.
ATS quoted Kengo as saying he was in Geneva for medical checks but did not elaborate.

The agency said Kengo had challenged accusations by the new Zairean government, which said it would issue an international warrant for the arrest of the former premier, sacked three weeks ago, because the national treasury was empty.
Earlier, a Swiss Foreign Ministry spokeswoman confirmed that Kengo had arrived in Switzerland with a valid Swiss multi-entry visa.
But spokeswoman Yasmine Chatila refused to say whether Kengo was still in the country.
"We know that he entered Switzerland in the last couple of days," she told Reuters. "But we don't know whether he's still in Switzerland."
The Swiss Federal Office for Refugees said it had not received any asylum request on Kengo's behalf.
Spokeswoman Nathalie Huguet of the Swiss Federal Justice and Police department said Berne had not been informed of any arrest mandate for the former premier.
Kengo has been widely accused of weakness in dealing with the Tutsi-dominated rebels fighting to topple Zaire's cancer-stricken leader Mobutu Sese Seko.

Switzerland was embarrassed over Mobutu's long stay in Lausanne late last year during which he underwent cancer treatment. After Mobutu left in November, the Swiss government announced it had denied him a re-entry visa.
